description: Every obligation of the pinned verification plan, bound to the named tests that claim it by VPO id. Generated by tools/acceptance (causa-acceptance bind); never edited by hand. missing = no test names the obligation; declared = a test source names it but no result was found in this run; bound = an executed result names it.

obligations.text: Every run must pin authoritative requirements and their source repository, commit, and content digest.
A modified baseline must be detected and require an authorized change process.
Each source obligation must have a machine-verifiable mapping to an implementation requirement, or a recorded scope disposition.
Detect omissions, weakening, negation, and role/value swaps, not only literal missing strings.
Agents must not approve their own exclusions, waivers, acceptance, or architectural exceptions.
Require verifiable operator or delegated-authority approval, bound to the exact requirement and baseline digest.
A required, non-optional job must verify baseline integrity, requirement coverage, approvals, and evidence before merge or acceptance.
Failing, missing, skipped, or bypassed checks cannot be reported PASS.

tests.testId: dotnet:Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.failing, missing, skipped or merely declared tests are never reported PASS
tests.name: Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.failing, missing, skipped or merely declared tests are never reported PASS

tests.testId: dotnet:Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.gates pass only on producers that succeeded in this run; absent, reused or failed producers do not
tests.name: Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.gates pass only on producers that succeeded in this run; absent, reused or failed producers do not

obligations.text: Before designing a component, discover existing Echelon capabilities, owners, supported versions, and contracts.
Reuse verified implementations; require an explicit approved justification for duplication.
Represent valid states, permissions, and transitions with typed F# contracts where practical.
Invalid or unauthorized transitions must be rejected before side effects.
Every PASS must cite the actual test, assertion, artifact, environment, and source SHA.
Distinguish PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, and NOT_RUN; never infer PASS from code presence or a mock result.
A reviewer distinct from the implementer must attempt to falsify high-risk claims, inspect requirements and evidence, and record gaps.
Reviewers cannot self-ratify operator decisions.
Critical tests must include a deliberately invalid case that fails for the intended reason.
Detect tests that pass regardless of implementation or verify mere existence rather than behavior.
Run fast deterministic domain/fixture tests frequently, provider contract tests at integration boundaries, and real provider and deployed browser tests at acceptance.
Live tests must never silently substitute mocks.
Record tool versions, pinned dependency SHAs, fixture seeds and digests, build inputs, CI run IDs, and deployed SHA.
Re-run must distinguish reproducible differences from environment drift.
Agent changes must be bounded to named requirements and paths; commits should stage intended files only.
Detect unrelated changes and require explicit review before inclusion.
Select tests based on changed contracts and dependency impact, preserving mandatory security, integrity, and release gates.
Batching tests for efficiency cannot bypass required checks.
Agents receive only the credentials, repository access, context, and mutation permissions required for current work.
Never echo secrets in logs, prompts, screenshots, or test artifacts.
Maintain durable, compact, machine-readable checkpoints of objectives, decisions, completed work, open defects, evidence, and next actions so agent restarts do not re-decide settled questions.
Route implementation work to the actual owning repository through its documented Praxis input folder and accepted grammar, never GitHub Issues.
Do not assume component ownership from its name.
Missing credentials, unavailable external verification, unsigned approvals, stale evidence, failed gates, or unverified deployed artifacts must produce BLOCKED or FAIL as appropriate.
An agent cannot override these outcomes with narrative.
The authoritative acceptance outcome MUST be computed from the evidence ledger, frozen baseline, required gates, requirements coverage, approved decisions, defect closures, and deployed SHA.
Agent-authored accepted fields are advisory at most.
Original Rehearsal 3 must yield BLOCKED; Rehearsal 2 candidate 45644a7 should yield ACCEPTED only if its actual ledger and evidence meet the frozen contract.
Include tests for false accepted flags, missing CI, baseline tampering, and unauthorized waivers.
Retain the demonstrated four-tier architecture brief as default guidance.
Do not add per-step Ordo architecture enforcement, typed agent records, or executable decision gates without a measured incremental correctness benefit that justifies cost and false rejections.
Typed domain models and security/acceptance boundaries remain mandatory where independently justified.
Prefer one long-running implementation agent with compact durable checkpoints.
Do not require structured handoffs by default.
Measure correctness and requirement retention after context compaction; use independent reviewers at release candidates.
Dependency-based test selection may prioritize but must not omit mandatory regression/security/integration coverage.
Do not restrict CI to infrequent checkpoints when intermediate changes can hide failures.
Require baseline tests that demonstrably fail on injected defects before trusting an experiment.
Select the latest *verified compatible release set*, not unrelated latest versions.
Confirm whether Dokimos 0.7.0 and Percepta have published artifacts; do not claim attestation from a set lacking its required components.
Resolve and verify Conditor scaffold defect SD-1.
Pin the exact set and require evidence for waivers.
An authorized human must resolve the write scope, Percepta release/waiver, DF-CAUSA-2026-0003 operator decisions, and frozen requirements/stack before a timed full-write rehearsal.
Agents must not self-ratify these decisions.

The application source, test assets included in production, release artifacts, Pages deployment, and runtime bundle MUST NOT contain the five R001 demonstration investigation datasets, event histories, golden states, or other prepopulated investigation content.
The data contract, schema definitions, type declarations, command/event catalog, migration rules, and synthetic test generators MAY be included; synthetic tests MUST NOT ship production records.
A fresh launch MUST display an accessible empty/disconnected workspace and an explicit Connect data repository action.
No implicit demo import or automatic fallback to bundled fixtures is allowed.
The user MUST specify or explicitly select the repository and permitted branch/workspace, and provide a scoped credential through a secure connection flow.
A token alone is not sufficient to infer a safe repository target.
Credentials MUST never be committed, bundled, logged, embedded in URLs, exposed in error text, stored in localStorage, or written into domain event files.
Prefer short-lived least-privilege tokens or GitHub App authorization.
In-memory-only credentials require reauthorization after reload.
Do not use an unrestricted personal access token by default.

The GitHub provider MUST check repository and branch permissions, validate file paths and manifests, and load only schema-compatible data through the full contract validation and F# history-admissibility pipeline.
Malformed, forged, unauthorized, or incompatible data MUST fail closed with safe diagnostics.
No data or repository mutation occurs on connect or read.
Creating a new investigation is an explicit user action; write/publish requires separately verified authorization, optimistic concurrency, and no overwrite of unread remote history.
The UI MUST distinguish disconnected, connecting, authorized-empty, loading, incompatible, access-denied, offline, and conflict states.
Never imply a successful connection merely because a token was supplied.
The app MUST create new Causa v1 file sets from the authoritative schema and engine without copying a demo investigation.
A new empty investigation MUST be command-created, schema-validated, replayable, and round-trip verified.

Build and acceptance tests MUST demonstrate a clean install with zero production investigation fixtures, no preloaded investigation records, successful authorized retrieval from a separately populated test repository, denial without authorization, malformed-data refusal, and successful create/read/write/reload.
The deployed exact SHA must be verified.
R001 remains an immutable experimental baseline.
The next rehearsal MUST measure external-data startup, authorization, read, write, and recovery independently.
Do not claim an external provider PASS based on mocked requests alone.
Preserve compatibility with the frozen Causa storage contract as a *reader/writer specification* without vendoring its demonstration records.
Version the contract and fail closed on incompatible data.
The data repository MUST be configurable and isolated from the application repository.
Treat repository content as untrusted even when authenticated.
Do not grant data access through publicly readable Pages assets.

The active demonstration catalog is the one named by causa-data `catalog/active.json` (historical-v1): exactly three historical investigations, Apollo 1 (AS-204), Apollo 11 and Space Shuttle Challenger (STS-51-L).

After an explicit Connect to that repository and workspace, the application MUST load all three through the full contract validation and F# replay pipeline to the states recorded in the catalog manifest, MUST NOT present any synthetic investigation as a catalog case, and MUST NOT bundle any of their records.
The five synthetic v1.0.0 fixtures remain the storage contract's test corpus only (STORAGE-005, STORAGE-007).
Define a typed F# investigation-data port shared by fixture and GitHub adapters.
The application/UI must consume the same result, error, cancellation, freshness, and provenance semantics regardless of provider.
Provider selection must not alter domain meaning or authorization.
Fixture adapters supply contract-compliant inputs; they must not implement parallel domain policy, state transitions, event reconstruction, causal inference, or confidence calculations.
The existing F# engine validates and reconstructs both fixture and real-provider data.
Support an explicit local fixture mode and real GitHub mode, using a documented, repeatable build/run/test command (FAKE or equivalent).
Fixture mode must require no network access, GitHub credentials, database, or external service.
It must not silently activate in a production deployment.
Display the active data mode conspicuously and never imply fixture data is live.
Fixture data must follow the frozen versioned Causa storage contract and be loaded through the same parsing/validation/reconstruction path as real data.
Maintain a machine-readable fixture manifest with IDs, schema versions, expected domain versions/digests, and expected error outcomes.
Do not mutate the frozen historical dataset.
UI and domain tests must not directly depend on GitHub, GitHub Actions, network availability, or credentials.
Real-provider tests must not silently fall back to fixtures or report mocked results as live success.

Supply a compact complete investigation with observations, competing hypotheses, supporting and contradicting evidence, provenance, unknowns, causal relationships, corrective actions, verification records, timeline events, and populated semantic color states.
Use stable IDs, timestamps, and deterministic ordering.

Supply an empty investigation; a completed/verified investigation; missing or incomplete provenance; unresolved and contradictory evidence; invalid event history; invalid schema; malformed or missing catalog; and missing investigation.
Expected outcomes must be explicit, including fail-closed behavior.

Model authorization failure, forbidden access, not found, missing branch (including GitHub HTTP 422 where observed), rate limit, timeout, offline failure, malformed response, retry, and partial transport failure.
Distinguish provider errors from domain validation errors.
Deterministically schedule delayed, reordered, superseded, cancelled, and retried requests.
A stale response must never overwrite the state of a newer request, and cached success must never mask a new authentication failure.
Request identity, active provider, credential generation, and freshness must be honored.
Domain: deterministic F# validation, reconstruction, state-transition tests; no external dependencies.
UI: browser tests using local fixtures for Forma screens, responsive layouts, keyboard/focus, accessibility, semantic palette, loading and failure states; no external dependencies.
Provider conformance: shared contract tests against fixture and GitHub adapters, with sanitized recorded real responses where appropriate.
Live integration: real GitHub requests against the authorized Causa data repository, validating catalog discovery, data transfer, reconstruction, expected digests, and errors.
Each level must have an independently executable command, CI outcome, and evidence.
A higher-level pass must not conceal a lower-level failure.
Document a single command that builds and starts a populated fixture-backed UI and a separate command for fast offline domain/UI/provider-contract checks.
CI must run offline deterministic checks without secrets.
Record execution time and failures by layer; set measurable performance budgets after baseline measurement rather than inventing targets.
Maintain sanitized, versioned observations of actual GitHub status codes, response bodies, relevant headers, branch behavior, pagination, cache behavior, and retry semantics.
Tests must detect fake/real divergence.
Do not capture secrets, private payloads, or sensitive headers.
Refresh observations when the provider contract changes.
At defined integration checkpoints and before release acceptance, run a real GitHub provider test against the approved repository and pinned catalog.
Confirm actual network communication, correct request-to-response association, three historical investigation reconstructions, expected versions/digests, and deployed application behavior.
Record repository ref, source SHA, run ID, and provider mode.
Never claim live success from mocks.
Public read-only catalog tests should not require a PAT when anonymous access is sufficient.
Authenticated integration tests use an approved secret such as `CAUSA_GITHUB_TOKEN` when explicitly required, with least-privilege read-only permissions.
Never embed or print credentials, put them in URLs, or include them in screenshots, traces, logs, or artifacts.
A missing secret yields BLOCKED, not PASS.
Fixture scenarios must exercise navy, teal, amber, coral, and ivory per UI-016, with textual state labels and contrast checks.
Capture deployed exact-SHA screenshots at required desktop, iPad, and mobile sizes for final acceptance; local fixture screenshots alone do not satisfy deployed acceptance.
Report failures by domain, UI, provider contract, or live integration layer.
A provider outage must not make offline UI/domain checks fail; an offline pass must not waive a failing integration gate.
Map each fixture and test to stable requirements and authoritative source commit.
Preserve obligations during rehearsal derivation; missing or weakened P0 obligations must fail requirements reconciliation unless explicitly approved as out of scope.
During development, agents should run the smallest relevant deterministic tests first, batch integration checks at meaningful checkpoints, and run the complete live/deployed suite before release.
Never skip a test required by an impacted risk or dependency.
Release acceptance requires green domain, fixture UI, provider conformance, and applicable live integration checks, plus exact-SHA deployed browser verification.
If the live provider or required credential is unavailable, report BLOCKED and preserve offline test evidence.

Before Connect, show an accessible, empty, disconnected workspace with the explicit Connect data repository action (EXT-DATA-002); after Connect, show the connected repository's investigations and the user's working copies, which for the active demonstration catalog (causa-data historical-v1, EXT-DATA-013) are exactly Apollo 1 (AS-204), Apollo 11 and Space Shuttle Challenger (STS-51-L).
Each card/row MUST show title, lifecycle, last recorded activity, and derived counts of hypotheses, evidence, and unresolved contradictions where supported.
Show severity and owner only if present in the domain contract; otherwise omit or explicitly label unassigned/unspecified.
Show the next legal action only if provided by F# policy.
Provide sort, selection, loading, empty and error states.
Opening an investigation MUST preserve its identity and context.
Show chronological event history with event type, actor/source where available, event timestamp, and domain version/sequence.
Provide filtering by category and a detail view showing before/after semantic changes when derivable.
Preserve immutable history; clearly distinguish event time from recorded time and order by canonical event sequence where timestamps conflict.
Selecting a timeline item MUST link to affected domain entities when possible.
Render only policy-authorized commands returned by the F# engine for the current version.
For prohibited actions, show a clear reason when the engine supplies one, without implying the action is available.
Capture required command inputs with validated forms and confirmation for destructive or irreversible operations.
Reject stale-version submissions, show domain fault messages safely, and avoid duplicate submission.
Keyboard invocation and touch targets are required.
UI MUST NOT implement a parallel policy engine.

Display source/provenance, capture/record timestamps, original evidence content or safe reference, interpretation, reliability/limitations where defined, and explicit links to supporting and contradicting hypotheses.
Never alter or overwrite the original evidence when interpretations change.
Sanitize untrusted text/URLs; clearly label missing provenance.
Enable navigation from graph, timeline, and hypothesis comparison.
Expose distinct states: clean, unsaved, saving locally, saved locally, queued offline, syncing remotely, remotely synced, conflict, failed.
Only claim remote synchronization after confirmed provider acknowledgement.
Show last successful sync time when known.
On expected-version conflict, preserve local edits and provide a recoverable compare/retry flow; do not overwrite remote history.
Frozen fixtures MUST remain read-only.
Never expose tokens.

Design specific recoverable states for no investigations, no evidence, unavailable projection, schema mismatch, invalid event history, offline network, expired authentication, failed sync, and conflict.
Every error MUST describe what happened, what data was preserved, and a safe next step.
Provide Retry only when it performs a real action.
Invalid histories MUST fail closed rather than silently rendering partial authoritative state.
Do not expose internal secrets.
Support keyboard-only navigation, visible focus, skip-to-content, appropriate landmarks, semantic status announcements, labeled controls, non-color-only states, and minimum usable touch targets.
Support iPad portrait/landscape, narrow mobile screens, desktop, 200% text reflow, reduced motion, and screen readers.
No essential operation may require drag-and-drop or hover.
Preserve focus and scroll context during transitions and WebAssembly handoff.
Graphs require equivalent accessible textual interaction.
Dashboard, graph, timeline, evidence inspector, comparison, and report MUST refer to the same investigation ID and authoritative aggregate version.
On a successful command, refresh dependent views atomically from the new projection.
Stale data MUST be identified, not silently mixed across versions.
Deep links MUST resolve or fail with a useful recovery state.
Use consistent Causa naming, icon, typography, navigation hierarchy, page titles, favicon, and accessible status colors.
The icon and startup behavior MUST satisfy WASM-LOADING-EXPERIENCE-REQUIREMENTS.md.
Navigation MUST distinguish frozen demonstrations from writable copies and expose current investigation context.
For each UI requirement, create tagged acceptance tests and a traceability map to underlying domain contracts.

Verify the three active-catalog investigations (EXT-DATA-013) load from the connected repository and replay, verify the five frozen v1.0.0 fixtures replay as the storage contract's test corpus, keyboard/touch paths, graph textual equivalent, timeline ordering, legal command enforcement, save/sync truthfulness, offline/conflict recovery, responsive reflow, report fidelity, and startup failure.
Test on deployed exact SHA; mocked persistence MUST NOT be represented as live write verification.
Missing verification is BLOCKED/UNKNOWN, not PASS.
The interface MUST have a deliberate, visibly colored Causa identity, not an effectively monochrome black/gray/white presentation.
Use these initial canonical palette values:
| Deep navy | Deep navy | `#14283F` | Primary navigation, masthead, structural emphasis |
| Teal | Teal | `#087F8C` | Primary investigation actions, active selection and positive workflow emphasis |
| Amber | Amber | `#E9A23B` | Unresolved unknowns, pending review and attention |
| Coral | Coral | `#D66B58` | Contradictions, material conflicts and critical investigation alerts |
| Soft ivory | Soft ivory | `#F5F3ED` | Main workspace surface and light backgrounds |
All colors MUST be mapped to named, semantic Forma theme tokens, not scattered hardcoded CSS declarations.
Use Forma components for surfaces, controls, states and focus treatment.

Define derived foreground, hover, disabled, border and dark-mode tokens only after measuring contrast; the five hex values are starting identity colors, not a guarantee of accessible foreground/background combinations.
Ensure WCAG AA contrast for normal text (4.5:1), large text (3:1), and relevant non-text indicators (3:1).
Do not convey lifecycle, confidence, danger, verification or sync status through color alone: pair color with text and/or icons, and distinguish causal semantics from decorative accents.
Use the same token semantics across dashboard, investigation views, timeline, causal graph, evidence inspector, report and startup shell.
Print/Folio output MUST remain legible in grayscale.

Acceptance MUST include actual screenshots from the deployed exact SHA at desktop, iPad portrait/landscape and mobile sizes, plus automated token presence and contrast checks, keyboard focus checks, reduced-motion checks and independent visual review.
Verify that navy, teal, amber, coral and ivory appear in appropriate populated states; absence of data must not force a misleading status color.
A grayscale-only interface is a failed UI-016 acceptance even if functional tests pass.
Investigation pages MUST present user tasks, investigation content, actionable statuses, and concise recovery instructions.

They MUST NOT display implementation explanations, storage schema versions, catalog identifiers, commit SHAs, replay/validation mechanics, framework versions, or infrastructure details as introductory paragraphs, persistent banners, or other routine UI copy.
Specifically, remove the catalog/replay paragraph beginning "The active catalog historical-v1" from the investigation catalog.
Where a technical issue affects the user's ability to proceed, show a short plain-language explanation and next action, with technical details accessible from Administration.
Preserve required investigation provenance and evidence source attribution within their domain views; do not hide substantive investigation facts.
Provide a separately navigable Administration page for system information and operational diagnostics.

It MUST show, as available and applicable: active provider and catalog, catalog version and source reference, storage/schema contract version, application and Echelon component versions, build/deployed commit, dataset validation and domain replay status, provider connectivity and authentication status without revealing secrets, and relevant diagnostic/error details.
Distinguish unknown, unavailable, failed, and verified states.
Never imply an unverified operation passed.
System diagnostics MUST NOT leak into investigation screens.
Administration is read-only unless a separately authorized operational action is specified.
Provide a separately navigable Settings page for user-adjustable preferences and configuration, distinct from Administration and investigation views.
Include only supported settings, such as appearance/theme, accessibility or display preferences, and provider connection preferences where authorized.
Distinguish a preference from a verified external connection.
Do not expose controls that cannot be honored.
Define persistence and scope of each setting (session, device, or account), show effective values, and avoid saving credentials in local storage or displaying tokens.
Provider authentication and configuration must respect the established security and read-only scope contracts.
Provide clear, accessible top-level navigation to Investigations, Administration, and Settings.
Investigation workflow actions remain in investigation context; operational information belongs in Administration; configurable preferences belong in Settings.
Navigation must work on desktop, iPad, mobile, keyboard, and assistive technology, with an identifiable active page and sensible narrow-viewport behavior.
Do not use an undifferentiated dashboard as a substitute for these destinations.

Add browser tests using deterministic fixtures that assert: (1) the quoted catalog/replay technical paragraph and equivalent implementation prose are absent from routine investigation views; (2) operational details appear in Administration; (3) preferences appear in Settings and behave according to their documented persistence scope; (4) navigation, focus, labels, and responsive behavior work; (5) no credentials or secret values are rendered or logged; and (6) deployed exact-SHA verification exercises all three destinations.
Tests must not simply check for page existence; they must verify content placement and user-visible behavior.
Preserve traceability and approved-scope handling in Praxis.
The global header MUST emphasize application identity and top-level navigation, not data-provider commit hashes or connection implementation.
The footer MUST omit build SHAs, component-stack inventories, and build timestamps; these belong on Administration (UI-018).

Investigation catalog cards MUST prioritize investigation title, actual domain lifecycle/status, latest meaningful activity, supported counts of open questions/evidence, and a clear Open Investigation action.
Do not show raw internal case keys as primary headings, "Expected lifecycle", duplicated declared/derived counts, or technical replay/verification explanations.
Internal identifiers remain discoverable where required for legitimate reference, provenance, and diagnostics.
Unknown counts MUST NOT be presented as zero.

A successfully fetched, schema-validated, replayed, or cached investigation MUST NOT be labeled "Verified" unless the domain explicitly asserts the corresponding investigation-level verification state.
Data integrity and runtime processing belong in Administration; investigation-facing badges MUST express only domain-authoritative conclusions, evidence status, or lifecycle.
Define disjoint labels and projection fields for technical data validation versus verified findings.
Regression tests MUST catch any conflation, including an investigation that loads correctly but contains disputed or unresolved findings.
Define a centralized, testable presentation-language mapping from typed F# domain/projection/error states to concise user-facing labels, explanations, and actions.
Do not let view templates or agents invent meanings, confidence, permitted transitions, or success claims.

Default labels: "Investigations" instead of "Historical investigations"; "Opening investigation" instead of "Fetching and validating the investigation"; "Status" instead of "Expected lifecycle"; "Investigation history" instead of "Replayed state"; "Explore changes" instead of "Open a sandbox copy"; "Apply change to draft" instead of "Ask the engine" when that is the actual action; "Change history" instead of "Engine decisions"; and "Discard draft" instead of "Discard the sandbox".
The wording MUST remain accurate to read-only, ephemeral, unsaved, and persisted states: never imply a draft was saved or a change was applied to the authoritative investigation when it was not.
Technical codes and provider details belong in Administration, except where needed in an explicitly requested technical detail view.
Preserve precise provenance and domain-specific terms where material.

Opening an investigation MUST lead to an Overview that answers, from domain-authoritative projections only: what happened and impact; current supported findings; supporting and contradictory evidence; unresolved questions; and next authorized actions.
Show unknown/unavailable information explicitly rather than inventing summaries.
Overview sections SHOULD link to Summary, Causal Analysis, Evidence, Hypotheses, Timeline, and Corrective Actions.
No AI-generated interpretation or unsupported conclusions may be presented as established fact.
Provide a dedicated Causal Analysis investigation section centered on the causal graph, with evidence and hypothesis inspection in context.
Reuse the existing Echelon workflow layout system under WDL-001..WDL-015, rather than hardcoded coordinates.
Graph node selection MUST reveal the corresponding authoritative hypothesis/cause and evidence counts, with navigation to the underlying records.
Preserve accessible text equivalents and read-only scope; do not imply graph manipulation changes the domain.
The application shell MUST expose persistent, distinct primary destinations: Investigations, Administration, and Settings (UI-020).
Within an investigation, secondary navigation MUST include Overview, Causal Analysis, Evidence, Hypotheses, Timeline, and Corrective Actions where supported.
Indicate current destination and preserve accessible focus/navigation on desktop, iPad, and mobile.
Do not flatten system settings into an investigation disclosure or use one oversized navigation list for both global and investigation-specific destinations.

Add deterministic fixture and deployed-browser assertions covering UI-022..UI-029: absence of technical metadata from header/footer/cards; truthful actual status versus expected status; technical validation never becoming an investigation-level "Verified" badge; mapped user-facing terminology; overview backed by the domain snapshot; causal graph invoking the real workflow layout engine; draft actions respecting engine authority; failure-state copy; and two-level navigation/accessibility.
Include negative controls for fabricated conclusions, unknown-as-zero, technical-language leakage, and misleading saved/verified states.
Record source requirement IDs, tests, exact deployed SHA, and independent review.
Do not mark unsupported features PASS.
Moving information out of investigation views MUST NOT delete operational observability or evidence provenance.
Administration MUST retain provider/catalog identifiers, build and component versions, data validation, connection health, and diagnostic codes.
Investigation evidence views MUST retain meaningful source attribution and traceability.
Settings MUST contain only supported user-adjustable options; read-only technical facts belong in Administration.
Apply role/access controls to sensitive operational information and never expose credentials.
Show domain-derived next steps for unresolved contradictions, missing evidence, pending verification, and corrective actions.
Link each to the underlying record and authorized action; never invent recommendations or treat unavailable data as no work.
Allow contextual traversal among evidence, hypotheses, causal assertions, corrective actions, and timeline events where actual domain relationships exist.
Use stable identifiers, accessible navigation, and explicit absent-link states.
Use an existing or reusable Forma-compatible detail inspector across diagram, evidence, hypothesis, action, and timeline selection.
Support desktop, iPad, mobile, keyboard, focus restoration, and consistent selection state.
Verify component ownership before building.
For domain-supported conclusions, explain supporting and conflicting evidence, linked hypotheses, verification history, and why unresolved findings remain unresolved.
Source all explanations from typed authoritative records and make missing provenance explicit.
Build UI-032..UI-038 from shared typed relationship, selection, inspector, and explanation contracts.
Reuse Echelon components; avoid duplicating domain logic or implementing unrelated subsystems for each screen.

Verify next-step authority, record navigation, responsive inspector accessibility, search/filter accuracy, completeness rules, deterministic offline demo, and source-grounded explanations with positive and negative fixture cases and exact deployed-SHA tests.
Trace all requirements through the documented Praxis input process; record approved exclusions explicitly.
Each build MUST use the newest available stable, published, compatible release of every applicable Echelon system at the time the build baseline is locked.
Applicable systems include Praxis, Ordo, Dokimos, Percepta, Forma, Forma Studio/workflow layout, Limen, Folio, and any actually integrated Echelon dependencies.
Discover the real owner and release channel for each; do not invent a release or assume every system is a runtime dependency.
Query authoritative package registries, GitHub releases/tags, or the owning repository's documented release source immediately before baseline lock.
Record checked timestamp, candidate release, source reference, and why it was selected.
Do not equate latest main commit with latest released artifact.
Prefer latest stable only when integration contracts and acceptance tests pass.
If the newest release is incompatible, fail the upgrade gate or obtain a documented, authorized exception for the newest known compatible release.
Never silently fall back to an old version.
Pin exact package versions and immutable artifact digests/commit SHAs in a machine-readable dependency manifest.
The lock is fixed for a given rehearsal/run and must not drift mid-run.
Re-resolve latest versions for each new rehearsal or explicitly authorized refresh.
Do not adopt alpha, beta, RC, unpublished source, or unverified local builds merely because they are newer.
Such use requires explicit approval, provenance, and the same compatibility and security gates.
Verify supported API/schema compatibility across Praxis, Ordo, Dokimos, Percepta, Forma, workflow layout, Limen, Folio, and other applicable systems.
Exercise integration tests, not just version-string comparisons.
Include the local bootstrap/build path and deployed browser where applicable.
Show resolved application, dependency, and build versions in Administration (UI-018), not investigation pages, catalog cards, or the global footer.
Versions must reflect actual loaded components rather than aspirational requirements.
A mandatory gate must verify the locked manifest against installed/loaded artifacts and compatibility evidence.

tests.testId: dotnet:Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.the lock gate fails when an installed artifact differs from the locked set
tests.name: Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.the lock gate fails when an installed artifact differs from the locked set

obligations.text: Missing dependencies, stale evidence, unverified artifacts, or skipped gates result in BLOCKED/FAIL, not PASS.

tests.testId: dotnet:Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.missing dependencies or unverifiable artifacts never yield PASS
tests.name: Causa.Acceptance.Tests.AcceptanceTests.missing dependencies or unverifiable artifacts never yield PASS

obligations.text: Every future rehearsal must reconcile VER-001..VER-010 with implementation and tests or an explicitly approved exclusion.
Work items must go through each owning repository's documented Praxis input path, not GitHub Issues.
Identify the workflow layout engine's owning repository, supported package or source integration, API, version, license, and constraints before implementation.
Document evidence of a working example and identify any required upstream changes.
Causa must not introduce a second general-purpose graph layout implementation or maintain fixed SVG coordinates for domain nodes and edges when the existing workflow engine supports them.
An explicitly documented temporary fallback requires approval and cannot be represented as satisfying this requirement.

Define a typed F# adapter that projects authoritative causal assertions, outcomes, hypotheses, cause roles (root cause, trigger, contributing factor, enabling condition), and evidence counts into graph nodes and relationships.
The projection must not invent causal claims, change domain states, or perform domain inference.
Causa owns graph semantics; the reusable workflow system owns placement, routing, spacing, and supported layout constraints; Forma owns accessible visual components and semantic styling.
Keep these responsibilities independently testable.
Node placement and edge geometry must be computed from graph input and supported constraints, not from hardcoded coordinates for specific investigations.
Layout must remain valid for zero, one, many, disconnected, and cyclic graphs where the domain permits them.
Layout must avoid unintended node overlaps, clipped labels, inaccessible connectors, and hidden evidence counts.
Edge crossings and visual ambiguity should be minimized using documented layout capabilities; do not promise zero crossings for arbitrary graphs.

Support desktop, iPad portrait/landscape, and mobile with accessible text equivalents, meaningful labels, keyboard navigation/focus, adequate contrast, zoom/reflow or intentional navigable overflow, and reduced-motion preferences.
Diagram information must not depend on color alone.
Render graph nodes and statuses using Forma-compatible components/tokens and the canonical Causa UI-016 semantic palette.
Colors must reflect domain-authoritative states; layout cannot assign causal or evidentiary meaning.
Given identical graph data, layout engine version, viewport constraints, and configuration, output must be deterministic within documented tolerances.
Stable node IDs and ordering must survive refreshes; avoid needless visual movement.
Where the workflow component supports interaction, node selection and navigation must resolve to authoritative investigation records.
Read-only rehearsal scope must not expose editing, drag-to-modify-domain, or persistence capabilities without explicit authorization.
Include deterministic graph fixtures: empty, single-node, four cause roles, dense evidence, long labels, disconnected graph, and permitted cycles.
The fixture provider must use the same domain-to-graph projection as the real GitHub provider (PF-001..PF-021).
